idea: An app that tells you what to cook with what's already in your fridge, before it goes off.

baseline.title: FridgeChef
baseline.pitch: Snap a photo of your fridge and get recipe ideas that use what you already have.

details.targetCustomer: Busy home cooks who want to waste less food.
details.revenueModel: Freemium app with a monthly subscription for meal plans and extra recipes.
details.competition: Supercook, Too Good To Go and recipe apps; FridgeChef stands out with photo recognition.

versions.title: Shelf Life for Shared Houses
versions.pitch: A shared fridge log for student houses that suggests group dinners from whatever's about to expire.

details.targetCustomer: Students and young renters in shared houses of 3-6 people.
details.revenueModel: Free for houses; paid placements from student grocery delivery services.
details.competition: Splitwise and group chats handle money, not food; nobody coordinates the shared fridge.

versions.title: LastBite Kitchens
versions.pitch: A back-of-house tool that turns a restaurant's near-expiry stock into tomorrow's specials.

details.targetCustomer: Independent restaurants and cafés with 10-50 covers.
details.revenueModel: Monthly subscription per location, priced against the food it saves.
details.competition: Inventory tools like MarketMan track stock but don't suggest what to cook with it.

versions.title: Expiry API
versions.pitch: An API that grocery apps plug in to suggest recipes from a customer's recent orders before items spoil.

details.targetCustomer: Grocery delivery apps and supermarket loyalty programmes.
details.revenueModel: Per-call pricing with an annual enterprise tier.
details.competition: Grocers build basic recipe pages in-house; none link them to what the customer actually owns.

versions.title: Use It Up
versions.pitch: A daily nudge that names one ingredient about to go off and gives you a 15-minute recipe for it.

details.targetCustomer: Busy professionals who shop weekly and bin food on Sunday.
details.revenueModel: One-off app purchase, plus affiliate links for the odd missing ingredient.
details.competition: Recipe apps start from the dish; Use It Up starts from the thing that's about to spoil.

versions.title: The Eat-Me-First Shelf
versions.pitch: A smart fridge shelf with weight sensors that lights up when food has sat too long, with recipes on a tiny e-ink tag.

details.targetCustomer: Gadget-friendly households who already own smart home devices.
details.revenueModel: Hardware sale at around $79, with optional recipe packs.
details.competition: Smart fridges cost thousands; this retrofits any fridge.

versions.title: Receipt to Recipe
versions.pitch: Forward your grocery receipt email and get a week of meals planned around what you bought, in spoil order.

details.targetCustomer: People who already shop online and hate meal planning.
details.revenueModel: Subscription at $3 a month after a free month.
details.competition: Meal kits plan for you but sell the food; this plans around food you already have.

versions.title: Fridge SMS
versions.pitch: Text what's in your fridge to a number and get back three cheap meals, no app or smartphone needed.

details.targetCustomer: Low-income households and older people without smartphones.
details.revenueModel: Funded by food banks and councils with food-waste targets.
details.competition: Every rival is an app; SMS reaches the people apps miss.

versions.title: Zero-Waste Private Chef
versions.pitch: A chef visits weekly, cooks from what's in your fridge, and leaves labelled meals for the days ahead.

details.targetCustomer: Affluent families who care about sustainability and lack time.
details.revenueModel: Weekly service fee, around $150 per visit.
details.competition: Private chefs shop fresh for every visit; this one sells the zero-waste promise.

versions.title: Shop Less
versions.pitch: Instead of rescuing food once it's bought, it stops you buying it: a shopping list that cuts what you won't use in time.

details.targetCustomer: Households that throw away a bag of food every week.
details.revenueModel: Subscription, pitched as paying for itself in groceries you don't buy.
details.competition: Leftover-recipe apps fix the problem after the fact; this one prevents it.

take.saturationReason: Cooking from what's in your fridge is a well-worn idea: several recipe-by-ingredient apps and food-waste apps already exist. Preventing waste at the shopping stage is far less covered.

similarExisting.title: Supercook
similarExisting.note: Finds recipes from the ingredients you tick off as already owned.

similarExisting.title: Too Good To Go
similarExisting.note: Tackles food waste, but on the shop side, selling leftover food cheaply.

similarExisting.title: Olio
similarExisting.note: Lets neighbours give away food they won't use in time.

pick.title: Shop Less
pick.pitch: A shopping list that learns what you actually eat and trims what you'd throw away, before you buy it.
pick.why: Every rival rescues food after it's in the fridge. Stopping the waste at the till is simpler to build, easy to measure in money saved, and nobody owns it yet.

alternatives.title: Fridge SMS
alternatives.pitch: Text-message meal ideas for households without smartphones, funded by councils with waste targets.

alternatives.title: LastBite Kitchens
alternatives.pitch: Turn a restaurant's near-expiry stock into tomorrow's specials.

followUps: A browser extension that flags overbuying in online grocery baskets
A council-run food-waste challenge with household leaderboards
